title: Spontaneous Association of the Terbium Cyclopentadienyl Complexes under Controlled Hydrolysis

synthesis.procedure: All operations were performed in a glove box under argon with distilled solvents (THF over potassium/benzophenone; hexane over K–Na alloy). A THF solution of sodium cyclopentadienyl (0.110 g, 1.25 mmol in 10 mL) was added with stirring to a suspension of TbCl3(THF)3 (0.482 g, 1 mmol) in THF (20 mL) and stirred for 24 h. A 0.42 M solution of H2O in THF (0.61 mL) was then added slowly dropwise with vigorous stirring, and stirring was continued for 3 days. The precipitate was removed by centrifugation, the solution was concentrated to half volume, and hexane (50 mL) was layered carefully. After 4 days of slow diffusion, a colorless microcrystalline precipitate of I formed and was decanted. The same tetranuclear cluster was first isolated as a poorly THF-soluble by-product during recrystallization of [Tb(η5-C5H5)2Cl(THF)] (II) from THF–hexane (1:2 v/v). Target hydrolysis of the in situ Cp-halide species gave I as a THF adduct in 90% yield.

properties.summary: No magnetic data. Luminescence was reported for solvatomorph Ia rather than unsolvated I.

material_class.structural_family: tetrahedral Tb4(μ4-O) cyclopentadienyl chloride cluster solvatomorph

synthesis.procedure: Solvatomorph Ia was obtained by recrystallization of complex I from THF. The molecular Tb4 core is essentially the same as in I, differing mainly in the arrangement of THF molecules. Photophysical measurements used a sealed 4 mm quartz cell at 300 K because the compounds are air-sensitive.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Recrystallization of I from THF afforded Ia as small crystals (0.5 THF per formula unit).

properties.summary: UV-irradiated Ia shows typical Tb3+ luminescence via 5D4 → 7FJ (J = 6–3) at 490, 546, 586 and 620 nm, with the 5D4 → 7F5 band most intense. Fluorescence and phosphorescence emission profiles are similar (delay 0.2–3.5 ms), indicating Tb3+ as the only emitter. Excitation fluorescence has a maximum at 270 nm assigned to the Cp ligand; efficient ligand-to-Tb energy transfer (antenna effect) occurs at 250–300 nm. Phosphorescence decay is monoexponential with τ = 0.85 ms (±10%) at 300 K.
